pr_body:
This change adds support for multiple concurrent requests, as well as loading multiple models by spawning multiple runners.  This change is designed to be "opt in" initially, so the default behavior mimics the current sequential implementation (1 request at a time, and only a single model), but can be changed by setting environment variables for the server.  In the future we will adjust the default settings to enable concurrency by default.

By default, this change supports 1 concurrent requests to a loaded model, which can be adjusted via `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL`.

By default, this change supports 1 loaded model at a time, which can be adjusted via `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS `.  Set to zero for fully dynamic based on VRAM capacity, or a fixed number greater than 1 to limit the total number of loaded models regardless of VRAM capacity.  In the >1 scenario, we'll still perform VRAM prediction calculations to see if the new model will completely fit into available VRAM, but will prevent loading more than the specified number of runners even if they would have fit.  

This change also adjusts our GPU selection algorithm in multi-GPU scenarios.  If we can fit the model into a single GPU, we'll favor that over spreading it to multiple GPUs.

Note: system memory capacity is not taken into consideration in this change, so for CPU mode, setting max runners to zero could result in memory exhaustion and paging/swapping.

Fixes #2109
Fixes #1656
Fixes #1514
Fixes #3304 
Fixes #961 
Fixes #3507

I've updated the description above to better describe how this works.  There are 2 layers of concurrency introduced by this change.  One layer is leveraging the parallelism support in llama.cpp to process multiple concurrent requests against a single loaded model.  The other layer is starting multiple subprocesses to handle multiple models, up to the limits of VRAM capacity.

Once this merges, we'll be eager to have folks try out the multiple model loading by setting `OLLAMA_MAX_RUNNERS` to zero or a number greater than 1 and let us know if you hit any snags.

@alexander-potemkin we don't currently have any limits to the number of client connections.  I don't believe we have wired up any sort of expiration/timeout setting on the server side, although I haven't tested how long a client could theoretically be waiting.  The current code does not implement a formal queue mechanism to guarantee ordering for pending requests, it's based on locks and signaling, so it's random which waiting request would get unblocked when a prior request is completed.  I think adding a FIFO is something we could look at adding incrementally in the future.

Slight correction to the above.  I just updated the implementation for concurrent requests to a single model to use a semaphore package that does FIFO for blocked requests so that gets us 1/2 way there.   The logic for multiple models that exceed VRAM capacity however still uses a regular mutex lock pattern thus it will be random which pending request gets loaded next.  Refining that to make it FIFO will be a nice incremental improvement.
@dhiltgen , got it, makes perfect sense, thank you!

Note for people following along.  I've adjusted the defaults so this PR now mimics current behavior of a single request at a time, and a single model at a time, but allows you to set env vars to opt-in to the new concurrency.

> This change adds support for multiple concurrent requests, as well as loading multiple models by spawning multiple runners. This change is designed to be "opt in" initially, so the default behavior mimics the current sequential implementation (1 request at a time, and only a single model), but can be changed by setting environment variables for the server. In the future we will adjust the default settings to enable concurrency by default.
> 
> By default, this change supports 1 concurrent requests to a loaded model, which can be adjusted via `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL`.
> 
> By default, this change supports 1 loaded model at a time, which can be adjusted via `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS `. Set to zero for fully dynamic based on VRAM capacity, or a fixed number greater than 1 to limit the total number of loaded models regardless of VRAM capacity. In the >1 scenario, we'll still perform VRAM prediction calculations to see if the new model will completely fit into available VRAM, but will prevent loading more than the specified number of runners even if they would have fit.
> 
> This change also adjusts our GPU selection algorithm in multi-GPU scenarios. If we can fit the model into a single GPU, we'll favor that over spreading it to multiple GPUs.
> 
> Note: system memory capacity is not taken into consideration in this change, so for CPU mode, setting max runners to zero could result in memory exhaustion and paging/swapping.
> 
> Fixes #2109 Fixes #1656 Fixes #1514 Fixes #3304 Fixes #961 Fixes #3507

There are 2 levels of concurrency which make this a little complicated.

OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS controls how many models can be loaded at the same time.  You could set that to 3 and if 3 models fit in VRAM, we'd load 3, but attempting to load a 4th would block until one of the others is finished processing, even if it would have fit in VRAM.  If you didn't update OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL then each model could only handle 1 client request at a time (so 3 different clients could each talk to one of the loaded models at the same time in this example).

For OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS, anything less than 1 wouldn't make sense (zero models?) so we map that to "unlimited" and just use the VRAM calculations. 

We'll probably hold off updating the README for the moment as this UX may change as folks test the feature and give feedback.  Ultimately we want to adjust the defaults so you never have to use these settings to get concurrent behavior.   You could start with `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=0` and `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=4` as an initial setting and experiment with your GPUs and models and see how it performs.

This change is designed to be "opt in" initially, so the default behavior mimics the current sequential implementation (1 request at a time, and only a single model), but can be changed by setting environment variables for the server. In the >1 scenario, we'll still perform VRAM prediction calculations to see if the new model will completely fit into available VRAM, but will prevent loading more than the specified number of runners even if they would have fit.

issue_context.title: Try to use only 1 GPU if possible
issue_context.body:
I have two GPUs: an RTX 3090 and a 2060. `ollama` tries to split the load among both, but due to communication speed between the cards being significantly slower than within a GPU, this is counterproductive. Would be great to prioritize using the first GPU only, if it alone has enough VRAM to fit the model.

Here are the results of a small experiment:

Model: `solar:q4_0`

- RTX 3090 alone:
  - 350 W: 81 t/s
  - 280W: 79 t/s
- RTX 3090 (280/350 W) and RTX 2060 (128/160 W):
  - 31.5 t/s

To do the test I just changed the value of `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`  from `0,1` to `0`.
